source: workflow wf_aefdf80e-d22 (probe-early-discovery): each lens's returned observations + an independent skeptic's re-derivation verdicts. Verbatim agent outputs; interpretation lives in analysis/notes/.

obs.lens: Two external witnesses with no transcript: collusion-wiki full logs (multi-clock wiki saves) and the urlquery agent-activity catalog (scan-report timestamps per data source)

observations.statement: No physically required clock ordering is violated inside collusion-wiki. The 5 checked orderings are request<=success, request<=write_date, request<=archived_at, success<=archived_at and write_date<=archived_at. Much of this agreement is by construction: time, write_date and request_time are identical on every row, so they are one clock written three times.
observations.numbers: Violations 0/14482, 0/14482, 0/14482, 0/14585, 0/14591; Wilson upper bound 0.0003 each. time==write_date 14591/14591; time==request_time 14482/14482. success_time - request_time values {0: 12792, 1: 1689, 2: 1}, n=14482. Deletes: success - request {0: 4746, 1: 470}; clock_delta_seconds mismatches 0/5216.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The export joined request-log rows to saves by exact time equality and passed its own 'revision order failures = 0' check. Only success_time (0-2 s) and archived_at are independent of the save time.

observations.statement: POST-HOC. RCS commit order (the 1.N storage sequence) disagrees with timestamp order on 72 adjacent pairs, all on 4 heavily edited shared pages. All inversions are 1-5 s, and nearly every inverted pair involves two different labels and ip16.
observations.numbers: 72/10012 = 0.0072, Wilson [0.0057, 0.0090]; page-clustered [0.000, 0.015], 1453 pages. 59 inversions exceed 1 s. Magnitudes {-1: 13, -2: 29, -3: 28, -4: 1, -5: 1}. Labels differ in 70/72 pairs, ip16 differs in 71/72. Separately, 414/14591 revisions on 5 pages have an RCS minor number different from seq.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Concurrent saves to the same page: the timestamp is taken before the commit lock, so commit order and timestamp order can swap by a few seconds. This is a race, not fabrication.

observations.statement: When a wiki page first names a catalog data source, a urlquery report for that same source in the preceding hour is far more common than at nearby shifted times or with sources permuted. The two independent witnesses agree on which source was being worked when.
observations.numbers: Before-window at 1 h: 0.566 [0.481, 0.655], n=3116 events on 2223 pages (page-clustered). Nulls: +-7/14 d shift 0.000 [0.000, 0.001]; source permutation 0.233 [0.182, 0.291]; post-hoc local +-2h/4h/1d 0.307 [0.264, 0.352]. Excess over the local null 0.259 [0.217, 0.303]; over the permutation null 0.332 [0.298, 0.365]. Excess over the local null at 24 h: 0.147 [0.140, 0.153]. Per source at 1 h: SEC county 0.423 [0.396, 0.445] (n=1432); USAspending 0.369 (n=165); MAX 0.393 (n=78); Clark 0.675 (n=60); IHME 0.595 (n=44).
observations.mechanical_explanation: This is campaign-level co-activity, not a link from a specific claim to a specific fetch. SEC county data is 1432 of the 3116 events, and all 455 of its reports fall on one UTC day. 8 of the 52 catalog methods were chosen partly from wiki content (urlquery_methods_with_wiki_in_reason). That makes source selection wiki-informed, though the report times are a census of each query.

observations.statement: Directionality is weak. A source report is only slightly more likely before a wiki mention than after it, and a urlquery burst is only slightly more likely to be followed by a wiki mention than the local null predicts.
observations.numbers: Forward, before minus after: 0.042 [0.010, 0.078] at 1 h; 0.159 [0.115, 0.204] at 24 h (n=3116, 2223 pages). Reverse, burst followed by a wiki mention within 1 h: 0.085 [0.019, 0.159], local null 0.045, excess 0.040 [0.007, 0.079] (n=4935 bursts, 131 source-days). Reverse excess at 24 h: 0.031 [-0.015, 0.085].
observations.mechanical_explanation: Both witnesses record overlapping streams of activity on the same source (median lag back to the prior report 971 s, forward to the next report 491.5 s), so there is no clean fetch-then-write ordering.

observations.statement: urlquery coverage depends on the source. For DataUSA and the US Census API, wiki mentions are almost never preceded by a report, so a missing report is not evidence that a claimed fetch was fabricated.
observations.numbers: DataUSA before-window at 1 h: 0.038 [0.028, 0.049], n=1259 events on 1203 pages; 91 DataUSA reports in the catalog in total. US Census API: 0/58 at every window; 5 catalog reports, 0 days overlapping with wiki mentions. 9 mention events belong to a source with 0 catalog reports (Yahoo CYBR).
observations.mechanical_explanation: The agents had other fetch paths (direct requests, other proxies), and urlquery is one optional route.

observations.statement: Bursts without regard to source (urlquery bursts vs wiki save bursts) line up only at the day scale. The alignment disappears against local +-2h/4h/1d nulls, although it looks strong against +-7/14 d nulls.
observations.numbers: 5 min window. urlquery burst has a wiki save nearby: 0.424 [0.231, 0.582], n=4060 bursts, 31 days; shift-null excess 0.312, local-null excess 0.035 [-0.008, 0.077]. Wiki burst has a urlquery report nearby: 0.678 [0.507, 0.806], n=2267, 28 days; local-null excess 0.060 [-0.014, 0.124]. At 1 h the local-null excesses are 0.015 [-0.022, 0.053] and 0.024 [-0.039, 0.087].
observations.mechanical_explanation: Both witnesses are busiest during the same campaign days (largest wiki save burst: 4621 saves on 2026-06-18, 17:42-20:52Z, with 414 urlquery reports inside it).

observations.statement: urlquery timestamps cluster at the same second, and almost all same-second groups contain a single data source.
observations.numbers: Same-second group sizes {1: 28350, 2: 3051, 3: 744, 4: 231, 5: 73, 6: 30, 7: 1}; 9810/38160 reports sit in a group of 2 or more. 3998/4130 multi-report groups have one source; 132 mix sources. Zero gaps 5680/38159; median gap 10 s. 60 s bursts: 8078, of which 3828 are singletons; maximum size 1006. Multi-report bursts: 3410 single-source, 840 mixed.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Most likely batch submission by programs: one script submits many URLs for one source at once. That is consistent with the custom_program / indirection classes. The second-of-minute chi-square p=1.3e-4 is not interpretable because the reports are not independent.

observations.statement: Narrated wall-clock times ('UTC', 'terminal', 'container') sit just before the save that carries them, whereas task-clock times are spread evenly around the save. This shows that the keyword classifier separates real clock readings from task-clock times.
observations.numbers: Real-clock time-of-day claims: n=854 new claims on 263 pages; median delta -84 s, page-clustered [-107.5, -64]. Counts in [-1h,0) vs (0,+1h]: 601 vs 95. Task-clock control: 344 vs 335 (n=6105). Unqualified times: 227 vs 201 (n=4238). Real ISO claims: n=31, median -46 s [-193, -18], 0/31 more than 60 s after the save.
observations.mechanical_explanation: None found. It also cross-validates that the wiki 'time' field is UTC to within about a minute.

observations.statement: The test 'a claim about an event cannot postdate its own save' does not separate cleanly for time-of-day claims. Of the 21% of real-clock claims that postdate their save, most are projections. Among past- or present-tense claims, the near-future rate is no higher than the task-clock control or a uniform unrelated clock.
observations.numbers: 180/854 real-clock claims are more than 1 s after the save: 0.211 [0.178, 0.245]. POST-HOC by tense: forward-looking 70/164 after the save. Past or present tense, not approximate: near-future band (1 s, 1 h] 7/125 = 0.056 [0.017, 0.100] (82 pages); task-clock control 37/550 = 0.067 [0.042, 0.095]; uniform expectation 0.042.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Times of day carry no date, so events more than 12 h old fold forward. The keyword tense tagging is blunt, and some times near a 'UTC' keyword are task-clock values.

observations.statement: Epochs printed from a real clock never postdate the save that carries them. Agent sandbox clocks agree with the wiki server clock to about 1-2 s.
observations.numbers: Epochs in prose: n=747 on 297 pages, median delta -1 s [-1, -1]; 10/747 = 0.013 [0.005, 0.025] more than 1 s after the save. POST-HOC: with a fractional part (time.time() form) 0/459, Wilson upper bound 0.008, median -1 s; without a fraction 10/288. Epochs in page names (vs the first save): n=396, 183 labels, median -2 s [-3, -2].
observations.mechanical_explanation: None for the 0/459. NTP-synced sandboxes are expected.

observations.statement: POST-HOC, definition chosen after seeing examples. Epoch-like stamps that postdate their own save are concentrated among round numbers (ending in 00, 01 or 99), which suggests agents wrote a guessed 'now' without reading a clock.
observations.numbers: Page names more than 1 s after the first save: round 26/55 = 0.473 (label-clustered [0.118, 0.660], 34 labels) vs non-round 5/341 = 0.015 ([0.000, 0.022], 153 labels). Near-future band (1 s, 1 h]: round 0.236 [0.088, 0.316] vs non-round 0.006 [0.000, 0.016]. Prose epochs: round 6/37 = 0.162 [0.049, 0.303] vs non-round 4/710 = 0.006 [0.000, 0.013].
observations.mechanical_explanation: Contaminated: the 20 inspected examples that suggested the roundness rule are inside the 26/55. Other possible causes: loop counters on a hand-picked base (e.g. ...000, ...001), or intended future markers. Needs a holdout.

observations.statement: Epoch stamps inside URLs postdate the save far more often, and mostly by more than a day.
observations.numbers: 39/370 = 0.105 [0.021, 0.231] page-clustered (81 pages) more than 1 s after the save; 30 of them more than 1 day after. Round 3/38 vs non-round 36/332.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Server-generated expiry tokens in signed URLs, and agent-made incrementing 'uniq=' sequences on a far-future base. This is why URL epochs were pre-registered as a separate class.

observations.statement: POST-HOC exploratory. Narrated task-clock to UTC mappings are not self-consistent at the minute level within a label.
observations.numbers: 482 new mapping pairs on 162 pages. Labels with at least 2 distinct pairs: 84; median offset spread 6268 s. Spread <=60 s: 3/84 = 0.036 [0.012, 0.100]. Spread <=600 s: 18/84 = 0.214 [0.140, 0.314].
observations.mechanical_explanation: The task clock may not run at wall-clock rate, a label may span several cohorts or episodes, or the nearest-time pairing heuristic may mis-pair. Untested.

observations.statement: The one exact urlquery report cited in the wiki is consistent with physical order: the citing revision comes after the report. Pages mentioning httpbin.org/base64 have an indirection-class report in the hour before in 7 of 8 cases.
observations.numbers: Citation (n=1): revision time minus report time = 8270 s. httpbin new mentions n=8 on 8 pages: before-window at 1 h 7/8, Wilson [0.529, 0.978]; shift-null mean 0.5 of 8; after-window 7/8.
observations.mechanical_explanation: n is tiny. There are 4568 indirection reports in total, many of them during the campaign weeks.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Unread-clock stamp detector: an agent-emitted epoch that is later than an external record of the save carrying it
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For every epoch-like token an agent writes (page name, prose, not inside URLs), compute delta = token - the server's save time. Flag delta > +1 s; the server reports 1 s uncertainty, and real-clock reads show median -1 s with 0/459 fraction-form stamps after the save. The round-number feature is a prior, not the test. Validate on a holdout corpus where the agent's tool calls are known.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Server-generated expiry tokens and incrementing ID sequences inside URLs; IDs that happen to look like epochs; deliberately future-dated markers; container clock skew (small here, median -1 to -2 s).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: the idea of detecting LLM 'now' guesses by comparing them against an independent server clock seems uncommon. Clock-skew forensics exist in general.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Source-level cross-witness corroboration: an independent URL-scan service records activity on the same data source within the hour before the agent writes about it
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each first mention of source S, test for >=1 scan report for S in [t-1h, t) against local shifted nulls (+-2h/4h/1d) and a source-permutation null; report the excess with page-clustered CIs. Use it only to corroborate (raise confidence when present), never to accuse when a report is missing.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Same-campaign co-activity by other agents or operators; scan catalogs whose query choice was informed by the wiki; sources the scanner rarely covers (DataUSA 0.038, Census 0/58), where absence carries no information.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: using a third-party URL scanner's public report timestamps as a witness for agent tool use seems novel. The general idea of corroborating logs across independent systems is not.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Narrated wall-clock residual: an agent's own 'current UTC' statement compared with the server save time
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Real-clock-qualified times compared with the save time: the median residual (-84 s) and the asymmetry within the +-1h fold (601 vs 95) show the agent read a clock. Present- or past-tense claims later than the save are candidate impossibilities, but at this resolution the near-future rate (0.056) does not beat the unrelated-clock control (0.067).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Projections phrased in the present tense; times of day with no date that fold across midnight; task-clock times sitting next to a 'UTC' keyword; approximate values ('~').
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: probably not novel as a forensic idea. It needs a dated claim format or hand labels before it can flag individual claims.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Storage-order vs timestamp-order inversion (RCS commit number vs time)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Per page, adjacent RCS revisions whose timestamps go backwards. Observed 72/10012 on 4 pages, all 1-5 s.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Concurrent writers on hot pages (timestamp taken before the commit lock). Every inversion observed here fits a race, so this mainly documents a false-positive source for any order-based consistency check.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: standard concurrency forensics; not novel.

could_not_measure: Claim-level linkage between witnesses: urlquery's public catalog has no URLs, bodies, values or submitter, so a specific wiki claim cannot be tied to a specific fetch or fetched value. Only source-level co-timing is possible.
Ground truth for fabrication: there are no transcripts or tool logs for these campaigns, so 'physically impossible vs the server clock' cannot be validated as 'fabricated'.
rclog clock on saves: recent_changes_time is null on all 14591 revisions. rcs_date and write_date on delete events are null.
Independent multi-clock tests on saves: time, write_date and request_time are identical by construction, so only success_time and archived_at vary independently.
Dated time-of-day claims: most narrated times carry no date, and events more than 12 h old fold forward, so an individual time-of-day claim cannot be declared impossible.
Validation of the post-hoc heuristics (tense keywords, roundness, task-to-UTC pairing): no hand labels and no holdout corpus. The roundness definition was chosen after seeing 20 examples.
Whether the task clock runs at wall-clock rate, which the mapping-consistency test needs.
Parallelism: no subagent-spawning tool was available in this session, and the probe runs as a single short process, so it was not split.

verdict.lens: ext_witness (skeptical re-derivation). I wrote my own scripts in <home>\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Swarms\5b3cb362-197f-4ccc-a976-2d9bb1ddbc1a\scratchpad (o1o2.py, o3_build/o3_rate/o3_profile/o3_cluster.py, o5.py, o6.py, o7/o7b/o7c.py, epochs.py, o11.py, tod.py) and saved their outputs in out_*.txt. I read the lens script only after I had my own numbers, to explain differences. The main event-set differences come from the lens matching URL-decoded bodies, using 13/16/19-digit epoch forms with no range filter, and requiring held history to start at seq 1 for page-name epochs. Net result: every hit and surprise reproduces in its raw counts. Two of them overclaim in how they are interpreted (O3, O7), and one is reported with mislabeled numbers (O3, per source).

checks.my_numbers: Ordering violations 0/14482 (req<=succ), 0/14482 (req<=write_date), 0/14482 (req<=archived), 0/14585 (succ<=archived), 0/14591 (write_date<=archived); Wilson upper bound 0.00027. time==write_date 14591/14591; time==request_time 14482/14482; time==success_time 12884/14585. success-request {0:12792, 1:1689, 2:1}. Deletes success-request {0:4746, 1:470}; clock_delta mismatches 0/5216. Revision seq order vs time: 0/10012 inversions, so seq is time-sorted by construction.
checks.problem: None. The 'by construction' caveat is correct. In addition, seq order has 0/10012 inversions because seq is itself time-ordered, so the export's 'revision order failures = 0' check is tautological.

checks.my_numbers: 72/10012 adjacent RCS-minor pairs with decreasing time; Wilson [0.0057, 0.0090]; page-clustered [0.0001, 0.0146], 1453 pages. Magnitudes {-1:13, -2:29, -3:28, -4:1, -5:1}. Label differs 70/72, ip16 differs 71/72. rcs minor != seq: 414 revisions on 5 pages. Per page: WillkommenImWiki 68, OAIResearchBridgeMay3X 2, AgentOurIvyProbe1781643368 1, StartSeite 1.
checks.problem: Minor overclaim. 'All on 4 heavily edited shared pages' is really 68/72 on one page (dse/WillkommenImWiki), plus 1-2 each on 3 other pages, one of which is a single-agent probe page. The race explanation is plausible but untested.

checks.my_numbers: My own patterns (raw substrings only, no URL-decoding) give 3044 new-mention events on 2063 pages; the lens has 3116 on 2223 because it also matches decoded proxy URLs. Before-window 1h: 0.555 [0.449, 0.671] page-clustered. Local null (+-2h/4h/1d) 0.305; excess 0.250 [0.204, 0.298]. Permutation null 0.224; excess 0.331. 24h excess over local null 0.146 [0.138, 0.153]. KEY CHECKS: (a) The lens's own per-shift rates are -2h 0.536, +2h 0.473, -4h 0.510, +4h 0.302, but +-1d 0.009/0.011. The local-null 'excess' is therefore driven by the +-1d shifts, which are near 0 by construction because SEC county's 455 reports all fall on 2026-06-18 (04:23-23:27Z). With a +-2h/4h-only null, my excess is 0.102 [0.087, 0.116] page-clustered and [0.042, 0.181] with 36 source-day clusters. With +-2h only it is 0.059; against the two preceding hours it is 0.030 [0.020, 0.044]. (b) My hourly profile, P(report in the 1h window ending at t+k h), for k = -3..3: 0.523, 0.526, 0.538, 0.555, 0.536, 0.466, 0.477. This is a broad multi-hour plateau with a peak of about 0.02 at the hour before the save. (c) Clustering by source-day (36 clusters) instead of page widens before-obs to 0.555 [0.094, 0.894]. (d) SEC county is 45% of events, 80% of before-window hits and 74% of the local-null excess. Its before rate is 0.996 and its after rate is 0.925 (lens). (e) Per source, the lens JSON shows these before/after rates: MAX 0.833/0.859, IHME 0.909/0.932, Clark 0.800/1.000. Only USAspending (0.764/0.558) leans 'before'. My per-source excess over the +-2h/4h null: SEC 0.123, USAspending 0.214, MAX 0.202, Clark 0.599, IHME 0.438.
checks.problem: OVERCLAIM and MISLABEL. (1) 'Far more common than at nearby shifted times' is false at the hour scale. The windows at +-2h and -4h score 0.47-0.54 against 0.566 observed. The 0.259 local-null excess comes mostly from the +-1d shifts, which are ~0 for single-day sources. The honest local excess is about 0.10 (+-2h/4h), or about 0.03 against the immediately preceding hours. (2) The per-source numbers in the statement (SEC 0.423, USAspending 0.369, MAX 0.393, Clark 0.675, IHME 0.595) are excess over the local null, not before-window rates. Placed next to 'Before-window at 1 h: 0.566', they read as rates; the true before rates are 0.994, 0.764, 0.833, 0.800 and 0.909. (3) The page-clustered CI understates uncertainty, because events on different pages share one campaign burst; the source-day-clustered CI is [0.094, 0.894]. The core claim reproduces: day/campaign-level co-activity that is source-specific (permutation excess about 0.33). It is not hour-level precedence.

checks.my_numbers: Forward before-minus-after 1h: 0.019 [0.010, 0.027] (n=3044, 2063 pages; lens 0.042 on its 3116-event set). 24h: 0.161 [0.109, 0.215] (lens 0.159). I did not re-derive the reverse burst direction.
checks.problem: None for the null conclusion: directionality is weak under both event definitions. The point estimate is sensitive to the event set (0.019 vs 0.042). The reverse-direction numbers were not checked.

checks.my_numbers: DataUSA before 1h: 48/1259 = 0.038 [0.028, 0.049], 1203 pages. 91 DataUSA reports on 8 days; 14 mention days, 3 overlapping (500 mentions on overlap days). US Census API: 0/58 events (17 pages), 5 reports on 3 days (2026-05-12, 05-24, 06-03), 0 overlap days. Yahoo CYBR: 5 events with 0 catalog reports under my pattern (lens 9, with decoded matching).
checks.problem: None material. CYBR is 5 vs 9 because of URL-decoding. 'A missing report is not evidence of fabrication' is a fair caution; the data cannot say the fetches were real.

checks.my_numbers: 60s-gap bursts within the wiki span (2026-05-24 to 07-02): urlquery 4060 bursts on 31 days, wiki 2267 on 28 days. 5 min: uq->wiki 0.424 [0.231, 0.582]; far-shift excess 0.330; local excess 0.036 [-0.007, 0.077]. Wiki->uq 0.678 [0.507, 0.806]; local excess 0.060 [-0.014, 0.124]. 1h local excess 0.016 [-0.022, 0.054] and 0.024 [-0.039, 0.087]. Largest wiki burst 4621 saves, 2026-06-18 17:42:33-20:52:40Z, 414 reports inside.
checks.problem: None. The local null includes +-1d shifts, which deflate the null, and the result is still null. A +-2h/4h-only null would make it more null.

checks.my_numbers: Same-second histogram {1:28350, 2:3051, 3:744, 4:231, 5:73, 6:30, 7:1}; 9810/38160 reports in groups >=2; 4130 multi-report groups, 3998 single-source, 132 mixed. Zero gaps 5680/38159, median gap 10 s. 60s bursts 8078 (3828 singletons, max 1006); multi-report bursts 3410 single-source, 840 mixed. NULLS I added: the source-homogeneity count expected from local temporal composition (sources shuffled within bin) is 2651 (day), 3561 (hour), 3689 (10 min) and 3899 (minute), against 3998 observed. Same-second clustering itself exceeds a uniform-within-bin null: reports in groups 3381 (60 s bins) and 5346 (10 s bins), against 9810 observed.
checks.problem: PARTIAL OVERCLAIM. Same-second co-occurrence is a real excess (9810 vs 3381-5346 under uniform-within-bin nulls). But 'almost all same-second groups contain a single source' is mostly compositional: shuffling sources within the same minute already gives 3899/4130 (94%) single-source, so the excess homogeneity is about 99 groups (2.4 percentage points). Single-source groups are dominated by UNCTAD (2389/3998). The batch-submission explanation is not distinguished from scanner-side queue batching.

checks.my_numbers: Independent classifier (fixed before I looked at outcomes): keyword nearest before the time within 30 chars on the same line, real = {utc, container, terminal, wall clock}, task = {task}, suffix ' UTC'/'Z' -> real. New per-revision claims, folded to [-12h, 12h). Real: n=738, 242 pages, median -77 s [-98, -60]; [-1h,0) 544 vs (0,1h] 87. With seconds only: n=510, median -64 s [-105, -46], 376 vs 53. Task: n=1835, 109 vs 110. Unqualified: n=6911, 372 vs 351.

The class sizes differ from the lens (task 1835 vs 6105, unqualified 6911 vs 4238) because of keyword lists, and the conclusion is unchanged. With fraction: 0/459, Wilson upper bound 0.0083 (exact match to the lens). Without fraction: 7/123. Page-name epochs vs first save: n=385, 173 labels, median -2 s [-3, -2].

checks.my_numbers: Page-name epochs: round (mod100 in {0,1,99}) 26/54 more than 1 s after the first save, label-clustered 0.481 [0.152, 0.667], 33 labels. Non-round 5/331, 0.015 [0.000, 0.022]. Near-future (1 s, 1h]: round 13/54 = 0.241 [0.091, 0.333]; non-round 2/331. Prose round 6/27 vs non-round 1/555. The 26 round after-save cases are 26 distinct epochs from 9 labels, 18 of them from the anonymous probier label ''. Their deltas run from 15 s to 1,333,479 s: 13/26 are more than 1h ahead and 6/26 more than 1 day ahead (e.g. 1782000000, 1783000000). Half the round after-save stamps are hours to weeks ahead, which fits hand-picked round identifiers (1782000000, 1783000000) better than guesses of now. Effective independence is low: 9 labels, 18/26 from a single anonymous label. It remains post-hoc, as the lens says.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Structured-counter vs visible-text recount
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each tool result, recount the quantity from the model-visible text or the call arguments and compare it to the harness counter by exact equality, pre-registered. Honest baseline I4: 2510/2514 (swechat) and 191/194 (cc_local). Rewritten or fabricated result text should break the equality unless the counter is rewritten too.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Truncated or persisted-to-file outputs, system reminders appended to result text, line-number formatting changes across harness versions, and Read calls with an offset or limit.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: I don't know of published work that uses the harness's structured copy of a tool result as a cross-check. Agent-observability tools may do this already.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Second-clock duration consistency
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check that each harness timer is at most the gap between the surrounding event clocks (call to end, turn start to end), with a tolerance set from an honest baseline before any outcome is examined. A reported duration longer than the wall-clock gap, or a gap with no possible execution time, would flag a result that was not produced by execution.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Parallel tool calls, clocks written at flush time rather than event time, millisecond granularity, skew between processes, and backgrounded commands.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: duration-vs-timestamp checks are standard in log forensics. Applying them to agent tool logs may be less common.

candidate_mechanisms.name: file-history-snapshot mutation reconciliation
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each successful Edit or Write on path P at time t, expect a later snapshot to show a version bump for P with backupTime >= t. Count claimed edits that have no bump, and bumps that have no claimed edit.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Snapshots are per user message, so edits coalesce. Paths outside the tracked set are missing. About 19% of files have no snapshot at all. Resumed sessions and Bash-made edits also break the mapping.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: this harness record seems unused in the literature I know of.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Session-tally recount
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Recompute each tally from the transcript (usage sums, tool counts, patch line sums) and compare. Report the disagreement rate with a session-clustered CI.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Tallies derived from the same transcript agree tautologically. Resumed or compacted sessions change the totals. Subagent tokens may be included in one count and not the other.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED

candidate_mechanisms.name: Cumulative counter chain
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check the chain identity total(n) = total(n-1) + last(n), and that ordinal counters only increase. Honest baseline I1b: 0.970, with breaks in 5/26 files.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Counter resets at compaction, rollback or resume, which plausibly explain the observed breaks (unverified).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED

candidate_mechanisms.name: Nested-subagent tally check
grounded_in: CC toolUseResult.totalToolUseCount / totalTokens / totalDurationMs (captured in extra)
cc_local workflow.json totalToolCalls vs subagent JSONL
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Compare the parent's reported subagent tallies with a recount of the nested or sidecar subagent transcript. Baseline I5: 190/190.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Nesting is absent in current Claude Code (cc_local), and subagent files can be missing or truncated.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED

candidate_mechanisms.name: External git witness of claimed edits
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Match the agent-claimed patch hunks to the committed diff, and report the fraction of claimed hunks that never reach a commit.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Human edits between agent and commit, squashed or rebased commits, and work that was never committed. Another lens (phase_c_commit_witness) may already cover this.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED

candidate_mechanisms.name: AI Village dual record of model calls
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Join an event to its turn and compare usage and the action between the two tables.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Events exist only for some action types, the join key is uncertain, and created_at is a row-insert time that can lag the event.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED

obs.lens: SWE-chat session- and checkpoint-level tallies as a second, harness-side bookkeeping. Each Entire-CLI tally (token/API counts, files_touched, checkpoint sums, attribution, timestamps) was reconciled against an exact recount of all 5,850 raw transcripts, conversations.parquet and commits. The lens also covers distribution shape, correlations and multi-axis outliers. Run as two parallel background stages (transcript scan on a 4-process pool, conversations aggregation) feeding one report stage. No subagent tool was available.

observations.statement: The harness token/API tally (5 integers per session written by the Entire CLI) equals an exact recount of the stored raw transcript, with tolerance 0, in nearly all Claude-Code-format sessions. The recount is distinct message.id over top-level assistant records with last-occurrence usage. A session counts as matched if the tally equals the recount over the whole transcript, a prefix, or a contiguous window.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Out-of-band usage-ledger reconciliation
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Recompute (count of distinct API message ids, summed last-occurrence usage) from the transcript and require an exact 5-field match with a tally the harness wrote outside the transcript at commit time. Allow prefix and declared-offset windows. Honest floor: 33/5701 = 0.0058 [0.0041, 0.0081] unexplained after correcting the join artifact.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Snapshots taken mid-stream (output-only mismatch, 7 of 14 Claude residuals), dev/old CLI builds, multi-checkpoint snapshot mixing in derived tables, OpenCode/Gemini messages whose token fields change after the snapshot. Blind to edits of tool-result content, since usage numbers do not change when a result is altered.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: using a harness-written token ledger as a witness-free check on transcript integrity (inserted, deleted or duplicated assistant turns) seems uncommon. Usage-based billing reconciliation is standard practice, but not as a transcript-integrity signal.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Provider cache-granularity plausibility check
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Every reported cached-input count must be a multiple of the provider's cache block. On the Codex/OpenAI path: 181/181 multiples of 128. OpenCode 569/619.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Providers or proxies with different block sizes, cumulative counters mixing providers (OpenCode through several providers), and Anthropic usage, which shows no granularity (49/4785 divisible by 128).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: a stateless arithmetic check on fabricated usage numbers. Likely known to billing engineers, but I have not seen it used for log verification.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Cross-snapshot inconsistency via ratio outliers
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Robust z (|z|>3.5 on ≥3 of 22 features) including ratio features (output/API call, tools/API call, seconds/API call). Rows assembled from two different snapshots are outliers at 9/36 = 0.250 [0.138, 0.411], against 59/4771 = 0.0124 [0.0096, 0.0159] for consistent rows.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Genuinely unusual sessions (very long, many prompts, automation), missing tallies encoded as 0, and early/dev harness builds. Recall is only about 25%.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: a generic data-quality technique. Applied to agent-log rows built from mixed sources, it may be new only in this setting.

could_not_measure: Distinct assistant message ids in conversations.parquet: the table has no message-id column, so the raw transcripts were used instead.
A recount formula for Copilot CLI (2) and Cursor (23) transcripts, nor for 2 unparsed files. 1 OpenCode transcript is invalid JSON and 1 Claude Code session has no transcript file.
The cause of the 33 residual unmatched tallies (26 with no 4-field match). This needs manual per-session reading.
Whether the harness ledger would catch a deliberately inserted or removed assistant message. No synthetic injection was run, so detection power is unmeasured.
Why prompt_count, session_metrics.turn_count and context_md prompt counts disagree (definitions not documented), including the repo-specific −7 offset.
Which attribution metric version explains the total_committed ≠ agent_lines + human_added cases.
Per-path reasons for files_touched entries that were neither tool-edited nor committed (1739 entries).

verdict.lens: swechat_tables. Independent re-derivation from scratch. My own scanner covered all 5,851 session_logs rows and 5,850 raw transcripts (scratchpad/rdx_tables/scan.py, a 4-process pool run in the background). I wrote my own table and commit joins (t*.py, plus conv.py for conversations.parquet). Outputs are in scratchpad/rdx_tables/out_*.log, and the numbers are consolidated in scratchpad/rdx_tables/rdx_summary.json. I read the lens script only afterwards, to explain why some n differ. My scanner did not classify 2 transcripts: one OpenCode file is malformed JSON (ses_3353a8139ffe...), and one Gemini file is a single-line {"messages"} file with no token fields, which would have classified as none anyway. T14 was cut off in the task text. I assumed it is the partial-correlation null from the notes and checked only a reduced version.

Prefix mechanism: created_at is earlier than the last transcript timestamp in 1664/1664 prefix sessions against 39/2772 full sessions. Messages past the snapshot: median 3, max 524. checks.problem: The numbers reproduce. full/prefix is off by one session (2772/1664 against 2771/1665), which does not matter. The lens's OpenCode prefix count of 8 probably includes the trivial empty prefix of the api=0 all-zero session or the malformed file. The problem is interpretation. The tally is a deterministic recount of the transcript's own usage fields. Part 2 of the notes calls it an 'exact, independent second bookkeeping', and that overstates it. Its only independent content is a commit-time snapshot, which makes later edits to usage records or deletion of assistant messages detectable. It says nothing directly about whether a tool result is real.

The tally equals the run of api messages starting at the first message at or after the declared line in 353. In the other 4, the window starts one message earlier, at a message whose records straddle the declared line (first_line < L <= last_line), so 357/357 are explained. transcript_identifier_at_start is found in the transcript 876/876. The identifier's message index equals the window start in 57/118 = 0.483 [0.395, 0.572].
checks.problem: Only the direction window ⇒ declared offset holds. checkpoint_transcript_start is also declared in 158 full-class sessions and 1 prefix-class session. In 154 of those 158, messages come before the declared line, yet the tally covers the whole transcript. So a declared offset does not predict per-checkpoint (window) accounting, and 'fully accounted for' should be stated for that one direction only.

observations.statement: Git can constrain roughly half of the Claude Code file-mutation stream. About 78% of mutation calls in linked sessions can be checked, and about 68% of all such calls sit in linked sessions.
observations.numbers: Sample: constrained 0.785 [0.757,0.811] = 17486/22282 successful mutation calls with informative added lines, 1057 sessions (repo-clustered [0.749,0.818], 135 repos). observations.statement: Most 'contradicted-looking' Edits have mechanical causes rather than suggesting fabrication. The main causes are partial-line edit strings, worktree paths, formatter-heavy languages and human or mixed edits.
observations.numbers: POST-HOC check of the first and last lines of new_string as substrings: contradicted-looking falls to 0.093 [0.074,0.114] = 1416/15164; 680 of 1512 contradicted calls with edge lines are then found. Worktree-like paths: 0.321 [0.207,0.405] = 326/1015 vs other paths 0.125 [0.103,0.149] = 1770/14149. By extension: css 0.397 -> 0.038 after the fix (104/262); json 0.244 -> 0.081 (72/295); go 0.211 [0.150,0.267] -> 0.161 [0.105,0.214] (614/2910); rs 0.198 -> 0.181 (163/824); kt 0/397. By the target file's attribution: agent_only 0.063 [0.047,0.081] = 459/7323; human_only 0.165 [0.121,0.215] = 752/4551; mixed 0.269 [0.221,0.319] = 885/3290.
observations.mechanical_explanation: 1) Edit strings that start or end mid-line break whole-line matching. 2) Path-suffix matching maps a worktree edit onto another branch's commit. 3) gofmt/rustfmt/prettier run by hooks or editors leave no Bash trace. 4) Humans edit between turns.

observations.statement: A small residual of contradicted-looking Edits stays unexplained after every flag. In 8 inspected examples it looks like honest later edits (a changed constant, a flipped checkbox, an extended comment). There is no ground truth to tell fabrication apart.
observations.numbers: After the pre-registered flags: 223 calls / 74 sessions. Also excluding same-path edits by another session of the same checkpoint: 182 / 52. Also applying the POST-HOC edge-substring rule: 53 calls / 31 sessions (mixed 32, human_only 11, agent_only 10; largest session 9 calls).

observations.statement: Write calls are almost never contradicted by the committed file content. Only full-content corroboration is informative: partial matches occur at chance level because common lines (imports, headers) appear in unrelated files.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The high decoy partial rate comes from boilerplate lines shared across repos.

observations.statement: The dataset's agent_changes field is a copy of the transcript's own Edit/Write inputs, not an independent witness. Its untraced entries mostly belong to other released sessions that the checkpoint's session list omits.
observations.numbers: Of 60995 entries in rows where every listed session was parsed, 0.856 [0.772,0.945] (52220) match a listed session's call on the exact key (path, old_string, new_string / content). Untraced entries: 4572 belong to another session of the same repo; 3738 belong to a session of a repo with the same name but a different GitHub owner (3738/3738 same name, 0 same owner); 452 appear in no released transcript (60 sessions); 13 match only on the looser key.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Entire attaches agent changes to commits by a wider window than checkpoints.session_pks. The same project also appears under several owners (forks or mirrors).

observations.statement: Most committed lines in agent-attributed files that seemed unexplained by the agent's calls are explained by sessions missing from the checkpoint's list. A small residual remains.

Lines explained only by calls made after the commit (agent_only): 182/252927.

observations.statement: When a commit SHA printed in an agent's Bash result (git commit output) resolves in the repo, git independently confirms it. The commit timestamp falls inside the tool call's own time window and the subject line matches.
observations.numbers: 1360 resolved claims, 510 sessions. commit_date in [call ts - 2 s, result ts + 2 s]: 0.993 [0.986,0.999] = 1351. author_date in the same window: 0.975 [0.964,0.985]. observations.statement: Coverage limits the commit-claim check. More than a third of printed commit SHAs do not resolve in the commit table, mostly for honest reasons, and listing-style SHAs (git log, git rev-parse) mostly do not resolve.
observations.numbers: 2178 claims in 634 sessions. Unmatched: 0.373 [0.307,0.437] = 813. Of these: a later history-rewrite command 356; the session has a commit_not_found checkpoint 303; the subject equals a same-repo commit subject 191; none of the three 266. git log / rev-parse SHAs: 15449 claims, 0.349 [0.298,0.407] matched in the same repo. observations.mechanical_explanation: Amend, rebase and squash change SHAs. Commits can be missing from the table. git log lists history from before Entire was installed.

observations.statement: 9 resolved commit claims have a commit timestamp earlier than the Bash call that printed them. This is the shape a replayed or re-printed output would have.
observations.numbers: 9 of 1360 resolved claims, in 6 sessions. dt values (s): -2713.0, -735.5, -158.0, -122.2, -78.7, -75.1, -71.4, -66.2, -27.7. 3 come from commands containing 'git commit'.

observations.statement: sessions.created_at is not the session start, so metadata-only time ordering of commits against sessions is invalid. Time order needs the transcript timestamps.
observations.numbers: created_at is later than the transcript's first event in 1200/1200 sampled sessions: median 0.797 h [0.655,0.910], p95 56.074 h. Metadata-based population order puts 6998 of 13424 (session, commit) pairs 'before_start'.
observations.mechanical_explanation: created_at appears to record when Entire first saw the session, not when the session began.

observations.statement: Linked commits mostly land within the transcript's time span or after its last event. Edits reach their target commit quickly.
observations.numbers: 4580 (session, commit) pairs in 1200 sessions: 2105 within the span, 2442 after the last event, 33 before the first event. Lag after the last event: median 5.415 h [3.292,10.978] (2442 pairs, 814 sessions). Edit-to-target-commit lag: median 0.253 h [0.195,0.335], p90 16.482 h (17486 calls). commit_date differs from author_date in 366/4580 pairs.
observations.mechanical_explanation: With the manual-commit strategy, the commit triggers the checkpoint, so commits after the last event are expected.

observations.statement: Attribution leakage: many agent Edits target files the dataset labels human_only, and most of those edits are present in the commit. The human_only label is therefore not evidence that the agent did not touch a file.
observations.numbers: 4551 constrained Edits target human_only files; contradicted-looking among them is only 0.165 [0.121,0.215] = 752. human_only '+' lines unexplained by agent calls: 0.890 [0.718,0.950] of 1778657.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Entire attributes per checkpoint from its agent_changes window, so an earlier checkpoint or another session's edit can make a file look human-only. Not verified.

observations.statement: Subagent Edits look somewhat more often contradicted than main-agent Edits, but the confidence intervals overlap, so the difference is not established.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Possibly more worktree use by subagents. Not tested.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Commit-claim window check
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each Bash result printing '[branch sha] subject', look up the SHA prefix among the repo's commits. Require commit_date within [call ts - 2 s, result ts + 2 s], plus subject and branch equality. Honest pass rate among resolvable claims is 0.993 (window) and 0.996 (subject), but only 0.624 of claims resolve. A fabricated output would fail to resolve, or resolve outside the window.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: History rewrites (amend/rebase/squash: 356 of the unmatched), commit_not_found checkpoints (303), unpushed commits, commands that re-print earlier commits. 266 of 2178 claims are unmatched with no flag. 9 resolved claims fall outside the window for unknown reasons.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Conceptually close to software provenance/attestation (in-toto/SLSA). Applying it to agent transcripts may be less common; no literature search was done.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Edit-to-commit line corroboration with decoy calibration
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Take the lines each Edit adds (new_string minus old_string, informative lines of 8+ characters, superseded lines removed). Look them up in the target commit's '+' lines and in the committed file content. Honest full match is 0.830 vs 0.003 for the decoy. The per-call 'contradicted' floor is 0.138, or 0.093 after the post-hoc edge-substring rule. That floor is too high for per-call alarms, so the check needs session-level aggregation and conditioning (agent_only target, no worktree, no formatter ecosystem). It covers about 0.532 of the CC mutation stream.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Partial-line edit strings, worktree path matching, hook or editor formatters (go/rs stay at 0.161/0.181), human edits between turns (mixed 0.269), other sessions in the same checkpoint. The residual is 53 calls in 31 sessions with no ground truth.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Diff-based attribution exists (SWE-chat itself attributes code to agent vs human). Using git as a falsifier of tool-result success claims, with a decoy-calibrated chance rate, may be less explored.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Write full-content check against the committed file
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check whether all informative lines of a Write's content appear in the committed file (file_attribution committed_version) at the first later commit. Honest full match is 0.836 vs a decoy full rate of 0.002; contradicted-looking is 1/2320. Only 'full' is informative, because decoy partial is 0.350.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Later agent or human edits before the commit (the 0.164 partial cases). Files never committed (Write constrained share 0.684).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Likely an obvious check, so probably not novel.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Harness-record vs transcript key trace (log integrity)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Hash (path, old_string, new_string) or (path, content) for each agent_changes entry and each transcript Edit/Write call, then match them. 0.856 of entries trace to a listed session. 452 entries appear in no released transcript (60 sessions). This detects transcript loss or truncation, but it cannot detect fabrication, because both records come from the same agent log.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Incomplete checkpoint session lists (4572 entries owned by other same-repo sessions), fork or mirror duplication (3738 entries from same-name repos under other owners), unreleased sessions.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Unexplained committed hunks (reverse check)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Find committed '+' lines in agent-attributed files that no Edit/Write/Bash text from the linked sessions, or from the owners of the commit's agent_changes, could have produced. This is 0.050 of agent_only lines, with 95 of 8129 files having zero explained lines. It could reveal mutations that were never logged.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Code generated by Bash scripts or codegen, formatters, unparsed tools (NotebookEdit, non-CC scaffolds), linkage gaps (the listed-session-only version gives 0.167), unreliable attribution labels.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED.

obs.lens: Internal accounting identities in the AI Village Claude Agent SDK stream (claude_code_messages / claude_code_sessions). Unit = run (sdk_session_id split at system/init, the loader rule): 314 runs, 53 sdk sessions, all runs used. CIs are run-clustered bootstraps or Wilson intervals over runs. Four rules were added after the first run of the script. Each is listed in post_hoc_rules and reported next to the un-ruled version.

observations.statement: The SDK's duration_ms matches the created_at span from init to result almost exactly, so for Phase A created_at behaves like event time with lag of tens of ms. Nevertheless, the strict inequality duration_ms >= span holds in only about 62% of runs.
observations.numbers: duration_ms/span: median 1.00003 (CI 1.00001-1.00009), p25 0.99927, p75 1.00103, n=211 runs. |duration_ms - span|: median 30.1 ms (CI 26.1-38.9), p90 230.6 ms, p99 2211.4 ms. Pearson 0.99999. duration_ms >= span holds 131/211 (Wilson 0.554-0.684). duration_ms >= union of call->result intervals holds 211/211 (0.982-1.0).
observations.mechanical_explanation: Insert-latency jitter of tens of ms makes the strict inequality fail in either direction. One outlier run (r031: duration 277325 ms vs span 509959.7 ms) is also the only num_turns mismatch.

observations.statement: Rows are written as content blocks finish streaming. The created_at gap before a block within one API response grows with that block's size.
observations.numbers: Pearson 0.930 (CI 0.919-0.948), Spearman 0.788 (CI 0.753-0.819), n=99701 block pairs in 241 runs. Median 162.1 chars/s (CI 155.5-168.0). No identical created_at among 244506 adjacent pairs. No adjacent gap under 10 ms. Minimum gap 17.5-46.2 ms depending on transition.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Streaming SDK output inserted per block. The minimum gap looks like a DB insert-latency floor.

observations.statement: Durations that tools report themselves fit inside the created_at call->result gap, with a median slack of a few tens of ms.
observations.numbers: gap >= reported duration: WebFetch 28/29 (median slack 33.3 ms, 11 runs), Glob 132/133 (44.0 ms, 26 runs), WebSearch 45/47 (27.6 ms, only 2 runs). Minimum slack -37.2 ms. Spearman(gap, reported): WebFetch 0.992, WebSearch 0.9995, Glob 0.096 (CI -0.063 to 0.350).
observations.mechanical_explanation: Glob's null correlation is expected: its durations are tiny next to fixed overhead. WebSearch has only 2 runs.

observations.statement: num_turns is a row-count checksum: it equals the number of user rows with null subtype (tool results plus compaction summaries) plus 1. It does not count API responses.
observations.numbers: num_turns == user rows + 1: 210/211 (Wilson 0.974-0.999); the only exception is r031. num_turns == API responses: 143/211 (0.612-0.737).
observations.mechanical_explanation: This is how the SDK counts. Parallel tool calls produce one user row per result.

observations.statement: Cost is an exact linear function of modelUsage tokens. Per-model coefficients recovered from the data alone reproduce every row, and total_cost_usd equals the sum of the per-model costUSD.
observations.numbers: Implied USD per million tokens. Opus: input 5.00, output 25.00, cache_read 0.50, cache_creation 6.25; reproduced 190/190 (Wilson 0.980-1.0). Haiku: 1.00/5.00/0.10/1.25; reproduced 172/172. Sonnet: 3.00/15.00/0.30/3.75; reproduced 141/141. Largest abs residual 1.2e-12 USD. total_cost_usd == sum costUSD within 1e-6: 265/265 (0.986-1.0).

observations.statement: modelUsage[main] equals result.usage plus one hidden main-model call per compaction. That call does not appear in the stream. Its input is a fixed 2 or 3 tokens (by version) and its cache read is zero. Its output tokens track the logged compaction-summary text closely.
observations.numbers: No-compaction runs: all 4 fields equal in 125/125 (Wilson 0.970-1.0). Compaction runs: n=65 runs, 595 compactions. cache_read difference 0: 65/65. Input difference == k x compactions (k=2 for v2.0.77, 3 for v2.1.38): 64/65 (0.918-0.997). Hidden output vs summary chars: Spearman 0.9975 (CI 0.9912-0.9993), pooled 3.734 chars/token (CI 3.687-3.79), per-run range 3.431-4.305. Hidden cache_creation / sum(pre_tokens): pooled 0.860 (CI 0.843-0.872).

observations.statement: Some logged API responses are missing from the result ledger. result.usage is never above the sum of logged per-response usage, but it is below it in 12 runs. In 3 more runs result.usage is all zero and the main model is absent from modelUsage, even though main-model responses are logged.
observations.numbers: result.usage input == stream sum: 196/211 (Wilson 0.886-0.956); result above sum: 0 runs. 12 runs below sum (non-zero), plus 3 all-zero runs (r085, r121, r140). In 6/12 a single logged response matches the deficit exactly in all 3 fields, and 6/6 of those carry a non-null stop_reason. Base rate of non-null stop_reason among non-synthetic responses: 131/65550 (Wilson 0.0017-0.0024). Excluding non-null-stop responses raises equality to 198/211.

observations.statement: Haiku and Sonnet API usage appears in modelUsage for most runs, but no responses from them are in the stream. These hidden calls are why duration_api_ms > duration_ms is common.
observations.numbers: Runs listing a non-main model: 172/211 (Wilson 0.757-0.862). Assistant rows in the stream: opus 168245, <synthetic> 21. Non-main pooled cost share 0.00496 (CI 0.0038-0.0064). duration_api_ms <= duration_ms: 39/39 in main-model-only runs vs 45/172 in runs with non-main models; 84/211 overall.

observations.statement: Cache-chain identity: cache_read(k+1) == cache_read(k) + cache_creation(k) holds almost exactly for consecutive responses, so context grows by pure appending. The next response's uncached input is about 8 tokens.
observations.numbers: Clean pairs: 59747/59804, run-clustered rate 0.99905 (CI 0.99858-0.99943), 190 runs. Image pairs: 4367/4570 (breaks have median diff -2104). Compact pairs: 0/933. Next-response input_tokens: median 8, p99 10. Clean breaks: 49/59772 at gaps under 300 s, 8/32 at 300 s or more.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Prompt caching of an append-only history. Long idle gaps and image handling break it.

observations.statement: Token conservation: per turn, the server-side context delta follows the chars appended to the log (the previous response's output plus tool results) with small residuals, including on a held-out half of runs.
observations.numbers: Clean pairs n=59804 in 190 runs. With thinking chars: Pearson 0.982 (CI 0.971-0.990), Spearman 0.986 (CI 0.981-0.989), pooled 2.610 chars/token (CI 2.586-2.638), per-pair median 2.535 (CI 2.508-2.57), p5-p95 2.078-2.87. Without thinking: Spearman 0.982, median 2.433. Pre-registered 3-term fit: R2 0.9663; |residual| median 49.6 tokens (CI 42.1-56.5), p90 201.0, p99 685.7. Hold-out: R2 0.9718, |residual| median 51.7, p99 667.7. |residual|/delta: median 0.023, p90 0.236, p99 0.887.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Expected, if the log faithfully records what the model saw. Thinking chars improve the fit, which suggests earlier thinking stays in context. Per-tool offsets exist: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob, Edit and TodoWrite have mean residuals of -92.7 to -193.8 tokens, while village MCP tools range from -40.3 to +35.7.

observations.statement: Stripped images ([IMAGE_REMOVED]) still have a recoverable token budget: the context residual per image is tightly concentrated.
observations.numbers: n=4543 image pairs in 64 runs. Residual tokens per image: median 898.8 (CI 896.7-899.6), p25 887.6, p75 901.4, p95 1007.1. 259 of 4543 fall in the 316-562 bin.

observations.statement: There are unlogged context edits: 30 non-compaction pairs where context shrinks and cache_read resets to the system-prompt prefix, with no compact_boundary row.
observations.numbers: Negative deltas: clean 3/59804, image 27/4570, compact 933/933. Of the 30 non-compaction negatives, 30 reset cache_read to 20401-21400; median delta -9249. By version: v2.0.77 6, v2.1.38 24.

observations.statement: Compaction pre_tokens is never below the last response's context, and the excess tracks the chars appended since that response. Its chars/token (about 3.77) is unlike server deltas (about 2.5), which suggests pre_tokens includes a client-side estimate.
observations.numbers: pre_tokens == last ctx: 0/933; pre_tokens < last ctx: 0. Excess vs appended chars: Spearman 0.819 (CI 0.725-0.898), median 3.775 chars/token (CI 3.766-3.796), n=863 boundaries in 92 runs.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Likely the SDK adds a heuristic token estimate for appended content to the last server count. This is not proven.

observations.statement: NULL: post-compaction context size does not track summary length. About 23k tokens of post-compaction context are not in the stream.
observations.numbers: Spearman(post ctx, summary chars) -0.135 (CI -0.274 to 0.030), n=940 in 100 runs. Post ctx median 26465.5. Post ctx minus summary chars/2.5: median 22975.1.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Post-compaction context is dominated by the system prompt, tools and re-attached material that is not logged.

observations.statement: ARTIFACT: per-row output_tokens in the stream is a streaming snapshot, not the final count. Only the result-level output total is usable, and at run level it tracks logged assistant chars including thinking.
observations.numbers: Result output == sum of last-row output: 25/211. Totals 9231390 vs 1603611. Output varies across rows in 8340/65529 multi-row responses; input/cache fields never vary. Run level: Spearman(result output, assistant chars with thinking) 0.9972 (CI 0.9941-0.9983), pooled 2.379 chars/token (CI 2.277-2.485), n=190.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The SDK copies message_start usage onto each content-block message.

observations.statement: ARTIFACT: failed-resume result rows ('No conversation found', zero duration) can land inside a preceding long run that has no result of its own. They break run-level identities unless they are excluded.
observations.numbers: Result rows not attributable: 54 of 265. Raw rule: duration_ms >= span 129/212, tool-union 209/212, duration-span min -12058911.8 ms. Attributable rule: 131/211, 211/211, min -232634.7 ms.

observations.statement: NULL: across resumes, context continuity is not preserved. The cache chain almost never holds from one run's last response to the next run's first response.
observations.numbers: 234 resume pairs without compaction: cache chain holds 1/234 (Wilson 0.0008-0.024); negative delta 88/234 (0.316-0.440); first-response cache_read zero 34/234.
observations.mechanical_explanation: A resume re-serializes the history and the system prompt, and the cache expires over long gaps.

observations.statement: The sessions table row is written right after the init message row. It is a second timing witness of invocation start.

observations.statement: NULL: the SDK stream has no linkage fields to test ordering against. Ordering checks that are possible show no violations.
observations.numbers: parent_tool_use_id non-null 0, parentUuid key 0, message_uuid column non-null 0 (of 244820 rows). Tool result before its call: 0. Next response before prior results: 0 of 65309 pairs. Block-type inversions: 0. Tool results created before the calling response's last row: 3002.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Per-turn token conservation (context-delta witness)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For consecutive API responses, compare the server-side context delta (input + cache_read + cache_creation) with chars logged in between (previous output, thinking and tool results) using a chars->tokens model fit per corpus. Flag turns with large residuals. Baseline: |residual| median 49.6 tokens, p99 685.7 (hold-out 51.7 / 667.7), n=59804 clean pairs in 190 runs. Each stripped image adds about 899 tokens.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Unlogged context edits (30 resets to the prefix), per-tool framing offsets (-92.7 to -193.8 tokens for 6 built-in tools), images, compaction and resumes. A crude chars model without a tokenizer. Length-preserving substitutions cannot be detected.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: Possibly novel as a fabrication detector for agent tool logs (UNVERIFIED).

candidate_mechanisms.name: Cache-chain continuity check
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Test cache_read(k+1) == cache_read(k) + cache_creation(k) exactly. It holds in 0.99905 of clean pairs (CI 0.99858-0.99943). A break locates where the server saw a history different from a pure append.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Idle gaps of 300 s or more (8/32 break), image handling (203/4570 break), compaction, client-side pruning, resumes (only 1/234 hold).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: Possibly novel (UNVERIFIED).

candidate_mechanisms.name: Log-vs-ledger reconciliation
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check the result row against the logged stream: num_turns == user rows + 1 (210/211); result.usage == sum of per-response usage (196/211, never above the sum); modelUsage[main] == result.usage + compaction hidden calls (125/125 without compaction; input 64/65 with it); cost linear in tokens (503/503 model rows). An inserted or deleted turn or tool-result row breaks one of these.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: SDK responses missing from the ledger (12 runs below the sum plus 3 all-zero runs out of 211), associated with a non-null stop_reason. Failed-resume result rows. Hidden auxiliary-model calls (172/211 runs).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: Ledger reconciliation is a standard audit idea; applying it to agent SDK result rows is probably uncommon (UNVERIFIED).

candidate_mechanisms.name: Hidden-call check of compaction summaries
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Per run, check (modelUsage[main].output - result.usage.output) against the chars of the logged compaction summary. Spearman 0.9975 (CI 0.9912-0.9993), per-run 3.431-4.305 chars/token, n=65 runs.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Only run-level (no per-compaction split when there are several). The token rate differs from tool-content rates.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: Possibly novel (UNVERIFIED).

candidate_mechanisms.name: Generation-rate and wall-clock timing consistency
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: The gap before each block should scale with its chars (Pearson 0.930; median 162.1 chars/s). duration_ms should equal the created_at span (|diff| median 30.1 ms). The created_at call->result gap should be at least the tool-reported duration (28/29, 132/133, 45/47). Rows written in a batch after the fact or fabricated would show floor-level gaps or a mismatched span.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Insert jitter (min slack -37.2 ms), streaming tool execution (3002 results before the calling response's last row), rare long stalls (r031). Applies only to sources with row-insert or event timestamps.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: Timing checks are standard; using streaming block gaps against content size may be less common (UNVERIFIED).

could_not_measure: Prices from outside sources were not used. Per-token prices are only coefficients implied by the data's own costUSD.
Per-response output tokens: per-row output_tokens is a streaming snapshot, so output can only be checked at run level.
Images are stripped ([IMAGE_REMOVED]). Only their token budget is checkable, not their content. Thinking signatures are stripped ([BLOB_REMOVED]), so thinking authenticity cannot be checked.
No uuid/parentUuid or parent_tool_use_id chains exist in this SDK stream. Chain-ordering tests are impossible here.
The identity and timing of the hidden haiku/sonnet calls: modelUsage gives tokens and cost only, with no per-call timing. duration_api_ms cannot be split into main-thread and hidden time.
Whether compaction pre_tokens contains a client-side estimate: only suggested by the 3.775 chars/token rate, not proven.
Detection power against real fabrications: there are no labelled fabricated examples, so only the honest-baseline residual and violation distributions were measured. No threshold was set.
Exact token counts of logged content: no tokenizer available (no new dependencies), so the chars->tokens linear model gives an upper bound on the residual floor.
Why 15/211 runs have logged responses missing from the ledger: an association with non-null stop_reason was measured, not a mechanism.
I did not spawn subagents: no agent-spawning tool was available, and the work is one sequential probe script (about 2.5 min runtime).
